meta.purpose: Estimator-level evaluation of the one-way false-positive-rate tipping point, as distinct from verifying the closed form itself.

scenario_grid.or_true_note: 1.00 is the true-null calibration cell and MUST be present. Round 3 item 2: the earlier assertion p1 < p0 silently excluded it.
scenario_grid.seed_note: 20261006; the v12 Monte Carlo used 20260926 and the two must not be mixed.

risk_provenance.hard_rule: The closed form consumes TRUE risks. Published arm risks are OBSERVED. Substituting observed for true understates the threshold by about 16 per cent at se = 0.90, p0 = 0.55, OR = 0.60, so nothing here may be presented as computable from published arm risks alone.
risk_provenance.unidentified_note: Neither has a validated estimate for the mRS 3-6 dichotomisation, so the inversion is not operational.

layer_A.name: arm-level two-parameter error
layer_A.use: the mechanism the closed form assumes; this is where 19.80 pp is verified

layer_B.name: mRS boundary grade error
layer_B.mandatory_check: record the effective sensitivity and the effective false-positive rate implied in each arm, and assert whether they are still equal across arms
layer_B.reporting_rule: cells where they are unequal are reported separately and are never pooled with layer A

expected_offset.scope: the specific common-process shape scenarios in v12 only. It does NOT bound every layer B cell, because layer B also varies the downgrade rate.
expected_offset.round3_item3: the earlier wording implied a general bound; corrected.

threshold_rule.delta_tip_definition: the unique delta at which the POPULATION observed odds ratio equals 1, that is, equal observed risks
threshold_rule.delta_sig_definition: the largest delta on the benefit side at which the two-sided Wald rejection rate is still at or above alpha
threshold_rule.delta_sig_boundary: CI UPPER limit; round 3 item 5, the lower limit is the wrong boundary while the observed OR is below 1
threshold_rule.delta_median_definition: the delta at which half of replications already have the CI upper limit reaching 1; reported separately from delta_sig

scan_axis.layer_A: delta itself, by bisection on the rejection rate, with delta_tip always evaluated as an endpoint
scan_axis.layer_B: the index upgrade rate a1, with the effective delta implied by the boundary model recorded on a separate axis

scan_must_include: the delta at which the population observed OR = 1, which is delta_tip
legality_assertions: p1 <= p0, compared with a 1e-12 tolerance
threshold_rule.legality_tolerance_note: Every bound is compared with TOL = 1e-12. At or_true = 1 the computed p1 overshoots p0 by 1.1e-16, so both `p1 < p0` and `p1 <= p0` fail on floating-point residue and silently drop the true-null calibration cell. A bare relational operator is not a sufficient fix.
threshold_rule.infeasible_cells: record the failing assertion and exclude the cell; never drop it silently

inference_rule.common_target: the between-group true log odds ratio
inference_rule.why_common: round 3: both confidence procedures must target the same population quantity, otherwise the two coverage figures are not comparable
inference_rule.true_null: or_true = 1.0 with delta = 0 gives the empirical type I error, which must land near 5 per cent
inference_rule.observed_null: the population observed OR = 1 occurs at delta = delta_tip; at that delta the rejection rate is a property of the sampling distribution, not zero
inference_rule.round3_item2: The earlier claim that the test statistic is identically zero and the rejection probability identically zero was wrong. Fixed population parameters fix the population OR, not the sample OR.
inference_rule.test: two-sided Wald on the log odds ratio, alpha = 0.05
inference_rule.coverage_layer_1: Wald CI for the between-group true log OR, uncorrected
inference_rule.coverage_layer_2: the same target after correcting for the assumed (se, f); the correction inputs are assumed and are never estimated from the same sample
inference_rule.power_scenario: or_true < 1 with delta > 0: the rejection rate here is a detection rate and must NOT be labelled a type I error

sampling_rule.procedure: for each cell draw x0 ~ Binomial(n, q0) and x1 ~ Binomial(n, q1) independently, with q fixed by the population parameters
sampling_rule.deterministic_vs_random: the population observed OR is deterministic given delta; the sample OR is random. Both are stored per cell as pop_observed_or and mean_sample_or.
sampling_rule.zero_cells: drop replicates in which any of the four cell counts is zero; record usable_reps against requested_reps
sampling_rule.insufficient_reps: a cell yielding usable_reps below 50 per cent of the requested count is reported as infeasible rather than summarised
sampling_rule.monte_carlo_error: binomial 95 per cent interval half-width on each rate, 1.96 * sqrt(r(1-r)/used)

outputs: bias: mean_sample_or and mean_sample_or minus or_true, on OR and log scales
type I error: reject_rate in the or_true = 1, delta = 0 cell
detection rate: reject_rate in the or_true < 1, delta > 0 cells, labelled as detection and not as type I error
coverage: layer 1 and layer 2, both against the between-group true log OR
delta_tip, delta_sig, delta_median and the gaps between them
per-cell Monte Carlo error, usable repetitions, and grid-refinement difference

self_checks.note: proves the or_true = 1 cell is reachable; round 3 item 2

self_checks.expected: pop_observed_or exactly 1 AND reject_rate materially above 0
self_checks.note: this is the correction of the round-3 error; a reject_rate of 0 here would mean the specification had re-introduced the confusion
the near-identity is itself the finding: the closed form already lands where the sampling test loses significance, so there is no large gap to exploit

self_checks.expected: None returned, with the failing assertion recorded
self_checks.note: round 3 item 5; an unguarded scan divides by zero on the far grid
